what_it_does: Large AI models (foundation models) are first pre-trained with many weights set to zero (sparse structure), but when fine-tuned on specific tasks, standard training methods fill in all weights densely, losing the sparsity benefit and wasting computation and memory during inference. This paper presents Phoenix, which keeps the sparse structure intact during fine-tuning by merging the sparse pre-trained weights with learnable low-rank adapters (compact parameter additions that adapt to the new task). Phoenix demonstrates that this approach preserves sparsity advantages while maintaining downstream task performance on Cerebras CS-2 hardware that supports unstructured sparsity.
